chunks: And it is narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, who said:

I asked Abā Ibrāhīm عليه السلام about a man who bought a sacrificial offering for his tamattuʿ, then brought it to his home and tied it up, but then it came loose and perished. Will it suffice for him, or must he replace it?
He عليه السلام said: “It does not suffice for him unless he has no ability regarding it.”

key_terms.هَدْيًا: a sacrificial offering intended for hajj rites
key_terms.يُجْزِيهِ: it suffices or counts for him legally
key_terms.يُعِيدُ: he replaces it or does it again

ai.seo_question: If a hady animal for tamattuʿ is lost or dies before sacrifice, must it be replaced?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a hady sacrificial animal purchased for tamattuʿ in hajj when it is lost or perishes before being offered. The Imam عليه السلام states that it does not suffice and must be replaced, except where the person lacks the ability to do so.
